senses.gloss:
भोग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, enjoyable, to be enjoyed, to
be used, (in the sense ‘to be eaten,’ भोज्य is rather
employed); to be endured or experienced; useful,
profitable; (in astronomy) to be passed; (आ), f. a
harlot, courtezan, prostitute; (अम्), n. what may be
enjoyed, anything that may be possessed or used, an
object of fruition, a possession, wealth, money; corn,
grain.
—भोग्य-ता, f. or भोग्य-त्व, अम्, n. the
state of being used or possessed, usefulness, profit-
ableness, enjoyableness.
—भोग्याधि (˚य-आधि),
इस्, m. = भोगाधि, p. 722, col. 3.

भोग 1. भोग, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. भुज्), any
winding or curve, a ring, coil; winding; the ex-
panded hood of a snake; a snake; the body; a par-
ticular array, an army in column.
—भोग-त्व, अम्,
n. the state of being curved or winding, curvature,
curvedness.
—१. भोग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for 2. see
col. 3), furnished with windings or curves, having
rings, ringed [cf. महा-भ्˚]; (आन्), m. a snake; a
mountain; (अती), f. a female snake-demon; one of
the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; the city of the
snake-demons in the subterranean regions [cf. भो-
गावती]; the sacred river of the snake-demons, or
a Tīrtha in that river sacred to the serpent-king
Vāsuki; N. of Ujjayinī in the Dvāpara age.

भोग 2. भोग, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. भुज्), en-
joyment, fruition; eating; use, application; usufruct,
the use of a deposit (Manu VIII. 149); utility,
advantage, profitable aim or object; enjoyment (of
women), sexual enjoyment; possessing, possession;
ruling, governing, protecting, rule, government;
cherishing, nourishing; suffering, experiencing; en-
during, feeling, perception (of joy or sorrow), pleasure;
suffering, passion; any object of enjoyment, that
which is eaten, food; food offered to an idol;
festivity, feasting, a repast, feast, banquet; income,
revenue; gain, profit, produce; money, wealth;
hire, the hire of dancing girls or courtezans, wages
of prostitution; (in astronomy) the passing (of an
asterism); the part of the ecliptic occupied by each
of the 27 lunar mansions or Nakṣatras, i. e. 13°
20° or 800°; (in arithmetic) the numerator of a
fraction (?); N. of a preceptor.
—भोग-कर, अस्,
ई, अम्, producing or affording enjoyment, procuring
food or pleasure.
—भोग-गुच्छ, अम्, n. hire of
prostitution, price paid to harlots.
—भोग-गृह,
अम्, n. ‘pleasure-chamber,’ the inner or private
apartments, women's apartments, zenana, harem;
[cf. भोग-स्थान.]
—भोग-ग्राम, अस्, m., N.
of a village.
—भोग-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by
enjoyment or by suffering.
—भोग-दत्ता, f., N. of
a woman.
—भोग-दा, f. ‘granting enjoyment,’ N.
of the goddess of the Piṅgalas.
—भोग-देव, अस्,
m. ‘having pleasure for a god (?),’ N. of a man
(Rāja-taraṅgiṇī VIII. 531).
—भोग-देह, अस्, m.
‘the body of suffering,’ the subtle body which a
dead person takes with him and with which, accord-
ing to his works, he experiences either happiness or
misery.
—भोग-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—भोग-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of possession,’ a person
in actual possession (of anything), the governor or
viceroy of a town or province.
—भोग-पाल, a
groom; [cf. भोगिक.]
—भोग-पिशाचिका, f. hunger.
—भोग-प्रस्थ, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
—भोग-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a poet.
—भोग-
भुज्, क्, क्, क्, enjoying pleasures.
—भोग-भूमि,
इस्, f. ‘land of enjoyment,’ the place where people
enjoy the reward of their works, Svarga or paradise,
(opposed to कर्म-भूमि, ‘land of works.’)
—भो-
ग-भृतक, अस्, m. a servant who works only for
maintenance.
—भोग-मण्डप, अस्, m. the part of
the temple of Jagan-nāth where the food to be pre-
sented to the idol is cooked.
—भोग-लाभ, अस्, m.
acquisition of enjoyment or profit; the gain or profit
made by the use of anything deposited or pledged;
welfare.
—२. भोग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for 1. see
col. 2), furnished with enjoyments, having enjoy-
ment, delightful, pleasurable, enjoyable, affording or
yielding enjoyment; happy, prosperous; (आन्), m.
dancing, acting and singing; N. of Satya-bhāmā's
residence (Hari-vaṃśa 8978); (अती), f., N. of a town;
epithet of the night of the second lunar day.
—भोग-वर्धन, N. of a country; (आस्), m. pl.
its inhabitants.
—भोग-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a
king; of a merchant.
—भोग-वस्तु, उ, n. an object
of enjoyment.
—भोग-सद्मन्, अ, n. the abode of
pleasure; the inner or women's apartments.
—भो-
ग-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—भोग-स्थान,
अम्, n. the body as the seat of sensual enjoyment;
the women's apartments.
—भोगाधि (˚ग-आधि),
इस्, m. a pledge or deposit which may be used until
redeemed.
—भोगान्त (˚ग-अन्˚), अस्, m. the end of
enjoyment or of suffering.
—भोगायतन (˚ग-आय्˚),
अम्, n. a place of enjoyment or suffering.
—भो-
गार्ह (˚ग-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, fit for enjoyment, to
be enjoyed or possessed; (अम्), n. property, wealth,
money; [cf. भोग्य.]
—भोगार्ह्य (˚ग-अर्˚),
अम्, n. corn, grain.
—भोगावली (˚ग-आव्˚), f. an
encomiastic poem, the panegyric of professional
[]
encomiasts or bards, eulogium.
—भोगावास (˚ग-
आव्˚), अस्, m. ‘abode of pleasure,’ the women's apart-
ments; [cf. भोग-गृह.]

1. भोगिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with windings or
curves, having windings or rings, curved, ringed [cf.
महा-भ्˚]; (ई), m. a snake [cf. कृष्ण-भ्˚].
[]
—भोगि-कान्त, अस्, m. ‘dear to snakes,’ air, wind.
—भोगि-गन्धिका, f. a species of ichneumon
plant.
—भोगि-भुज्, क्, m. ‘eating snakes,’ an ich-
neumon.
—भोगि-वल्लभ, अम्, n. ‘beloved by
snakes,’ sandal.
—भोगीन्द्र (˚गि-इन्˚), अस्, m.
‘king of snakes,’ an epithet of Ananta or Śeṣa.

2. भोगिन्, ई, इनी, इ, enjoying, eating; using, pos-
sessing; suffering, experiencing, undergoing; an
enjoyer, possessor, &c.; full of enjoyments, devoted
to enjoyments, indulging in sensual pleasures;
wealthy, opulent; (ई), m. a voluptuary, a king,
prince; the head man of a village; a barber; a
person who accumulates money for a particular ex-
penditure; (इनी), f. the concubine of a king or a
wife not regularly consecrated with him; epithet of
a kind of heroine.

भोगिक, अस्, m. a horse-keeper, groom (= भो-
ग-पाल).

भोगीन, अस्, आ, अम्, at the end of a comp. [cf.
मातृ-भोगीण].
